questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Mark the correct statements (s).
(i) Manganese exhibits +7 oxidation state
(ii) Zinc forms coloured ions
(iii) $[ Co{F}_{6}{]}^{3 -}$ is diamagnetic
(iv) Sc forms +4 oxidation state
(v) Zn exhibits only +2 oxidation state
questions.solution:
Outer electronic configuration of Mn is $3d^{5}4s^{2}$ which means it exhibits +7 oxidation state
Zinc does not form coloured ions as it has completely filled $3d^{10}4s^{2}$ configuration.
In $[ Co{F}_{6}{]}^{3 -}, Co^{3 +}$ is a $d^{7}$ system. Fluoride is a weak field ligand and hence it can not cause pairing of electrons.

Sc can form a maximum of +3 oxidation state as it has an outer electronic configuration of $3d^{1}4s^{2}$.
Zn exhibits only +2 oxidation state as this O.S. is the most stable one for it.
Hence i, v are correct while ii,iii,iv are incorrect.

questions.q: The amount of solute (molar mass $60g$ m$ ol^{- 1}$ ) that must be added to 180 g of water so that the vapour pressure of water is lowered by 10 % is
questions.solution:
Relative lowering of vapour pressure is given as
$\dfrac{p^{o} - {p}_{s}}{p^{o}} = \dfrac{{w}_{A}}{{m}_{A}} \times \dfrac{{m}_{B}}{{w}_{B}}$
As relative lowering of vapour pressure
$= \dfrac{p^{o} - {p}_{s}}{p^{o}} = \dfrac{10}{100}$
${m}_{A} = 60, {w}_{B} = 180, {w}_{A} = x$
So $\dfrac{10}{100} = \dfrac{x / 60}{180 / 18}$
$\dfrac{1}{10} = \dfrac{x / 60}{10}$
It mean $60g$ of the solute must be added to $180g$ of water so that the vapour pressure of water is lowered by 10 %.

questions.q:

disproportionation is not shown in
questions.solution:
I. $\begin{cases}{NH}_{4}^{+} & {NO}_{3}^{-} & \to & {N}_{2} \text{O} & + & 2 {H}_{2} \text{O} \\ - 3 & + 5 & & + 1 & & \end{cases}$

It is a redox reaction but it is comproportionation reaction. Since, different N-species are involved

Thus, it is also not a disproportionation reaction.

questions.q: The rapid change of pH near the stoichiometric point of an acid-base titration is the basis of indicator detection. pH of the solution is related to ratio of the concentration of the conjugate acid (HIn) and base $( In^{-} )$ forms of the indicator by the expression
questions.solution:
Let us consider the formation of a salt of a weak acid and a strong base.
$In^{-} + {H}_{2}O ⇌ HIn + OH^{-}$
${K}_{h}\dfrac{[ HIn ] [ OH^{-} ]}{[ In^{-} ]}$ …(i)
Other equations present in the solution are
$HIn ⇌ H^{+} + In^{-}$
${H}_{2}O ⇌ H^{+} + OH^{-}$
${K}_{In} = \dfrac{[ H^{+} ] [ In^{-} ]}{[ HIn ]}$ …(ii)
${K}_{w} = [ H^{+} ] [ OH^{-} ]$ …(iii)
From (ii) and (iii),
$\dfrac{{K}_{w}}{{K}_{In}}\dfrac{[ HIn ] [ OH^{-} ]}{[ In^{-} ]} = {K}_{h}$
$[ OH^{-} ] = \dfrac{{K}_{w}}{{K}_{In}}\dfrac{[ In^{-} ]}{[ HIn ]}$
$log [ OH^{-} ] = log{K}_{w} - log{K}_{In} + log\dfrac{[ In^{-} ]}{[ HIn ]}$
$- pOH = - p{K}_{w} + p{K}_{In} + log\dfrac{[ In^{-} ]}{[ HIn ]}$
$p{K}_{w} - pOH = p{K}_{In} + log\dfrac{[ In^{-} ]}{[ HIn ]}$
or, $pH = p{K}_{In} + log\dfrac{[ In^{-} ]}{[ HIn ]}$
i.e. $log\dfrac{[ In^{-} ]}{[ HIn ]} = pH - p{K}_{In}$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
The number of electrons donated from substance(s) getting oxidized to the substance(s) getting reduced in the chemical equation for the following reaction is:
${\text{Cr}}_{2} {\text{O}}_{7}^{2 -} + {\text{Fe}}^{2 +} + {\text{C}}_{2} {\text{O}}_{4}^{2 -} \to {\text{Cr}}^{3 +} + {\text{Fe}}^{3 +} + {\text{CO}}_{2}$ (Unbalanced)
questions.solution:
Writing the balanced oxidation and reduction half-reactions, making the number of electrons same in them and adding both half-reactions gives us the final balanced equation:

$[ {Fe}^{2 +} + {C}_{2}{O}_{4}^{2 -} \to {Fe}^{3 +} + 2{CO}_{2} + 3{e}^{-} ] \times 2 ( oxidation )$

${Cr}_{2}{O}_{7}^{2 -} + 14{H}^{+} + 6{e}^{-} \to 2{Cr}^{3 +} + 7{H}_{2}O ( reduction )$

On adding both the reactions, we get,

${Cr}_{2}{O}_{7}^{2 -} + 2{Fe}_{}^{2 +} + 2{C}_{2}{O}_{4}^{2 -} + 14{H}_{}^{+}\overset{}{\to}2{Cr}^{3 +} + 2{Fe}^{3 +} + 4{CO}_{2} + 7{H}_{2}O$

Thus, $6$ electrons are donated from oxidized substances to the reduced substance.
questions.question:

questions.explanation:
Writing the balanced oxidation and reduction half-reactions, making the number of electrons same in them and adding both half-reactions gives us the final balanced equation:

$[ {Fe}^{2 +} + {C}_{2}{O}_{4}^{2 -} \to {Fe}^{3 +} + 2{CO}_{2} + 3{e}^{-} ] \times 2 ( oxidation )$

${Cr}_{2}{O}_{7}^{2 -} + 14{H}^{+} + 6{e}^{-} \to 2{Cr}^{3 +} + 7{H}_{2}O ( reduction )$

On adding both the reactions, we get,

${Cr}_{2}{O}_{7}^{2 -} + 2{Fe}_{}^{2 +} + 2{C}_{2}{O}_{4}^{2 -} + 14{H}_{}^{+}\overset{}{\to}2{Cr}^{3 +} + 2{Fe}^{3 +} + 4{CO}_{2} + 7{H}_{2}O$

Thus, $6$ electrons are donated from oxidized substances to the reduced substance.

questions.q: What is the possible product of the reaction in which $1mole$ of ${HNO}_{3}$ is reduced by absorption of $4moles$& electrons?
questions.solution:
Here, when nitric acid is converted into any of the nitrogen compound, the oxidation state of nitrogen is changed and for oxygen and hydrogen, it remains unchanged.

Let the oxidation state of Nitrogen in ${HNO}_{3}$ be $x.$

Then, $+ 1 + x + 3\left(- 2\right) = 0 ⇒ x - 5 = 0 ⇒ x = + 5$.

Now, after absorption of $4moles$ of electrons, the oxidation state of nitrogen will become

$N^{5 +} + 4e^{-}\overset{}{→}N^{+}$

Out of the given compounds, the compound having the oxidation state of nitrogen as $+ 1$ is ${N}_{2}O$.

Thus, here nitric acid is getting converted into dinitrogen oxide.

$1moleof{HNO}_{3}\overset{gives}{→}xmolesof{N}_{2}O$

Applying principle of atom conservation for nitrogen,

$1 \times molesof{HNO}_{3} = 2 \times molesof{N}_{2}O1 \times 1 = 2xx = \dfrac{1}{2} = 0. 5mol$
